title: Tool use
objective: See who does what in tool use: the model asks for a tool call, your code runs it and sends the result back, and only then can the model answer.

sources.title: Claude Platform docs: Tool use with Claude (the model returns a tool_use block; your code runs client tools and sends back a tool_result)
Anthropic: Building effective agents ("The basic building block of agentic systems is an LLM enhanced with augmentations such as retrieval, tools, and memory")

simplifies: The model here is a script with fixed rules, not a real AI: a real model's choices vary between runs, and it might give up, ask for help or retry differently. In the real API the model's request is a tool_use block and your code replies with a tool_result block.

challenges.title: No tool, no facts
challenges.prompt: The model has no order_status tool. Get a right answer, with no made-up ones.

predict.prompt: The model has no tool, and the user asks about their own order. What will it say?

options.text: Something general, like "orders usually arrive in 3 to 5 days"
options.explanation: Right. It can't see your order system, so a general guess is all it has.
This script answers from general knowledge; real models may also guess.

challenges.hint: What would let the model see the live status?
challenges.explain: With the tool, the model can ask for the live status instead of guessing from general knowledge.

challenges.title: Nobody runs the call
challenges.prompt: The model has the tool, but your code doesn't run the calls it asks for. Get a right answer.
challenges.hint: The model asks. Who has to do the work?
challenges.explain: The model only asks for the call; your code runs it and sends the result back. Without that, no result ever comes.

quiz.prompt: Who actually runs a tool the model asks for?

options.text: The model, inside its own reply
options.explanation: The model only asks; it can't run your code.

options.text: The user, by clicking a button
options.explanation: Your app runs it, usually without the user doing anything.
Right. The model returns a tool_use request; your code executes it and returns a tool_result.

quiz.prompt: How does the model decide whether to call a tool?

options.text: It always calls every tool once
options.explanation: It calls a tool only when the request needs it.

options.text: From the user's request and the tool's description
options.explanation: Right. That's why clear tool descriptions matter.
It reads the request and the descriptions it was given.
